question.problem:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}+3{y}^{′}-4y=f(x).
$$

The corresponding homogeneous equation has the fundamental solutions ${y}_{1}(x)={e}^{x}$ and ${y}_{2}(x)={e}^{-4x}:$

According to the method of variation of parameters, we seek a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={{field-1}}
$$

where ${u}_{1}={u}_{1}(x),{u}_{2}={u}_{2}(x),$ that satisfies the constraint

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}(x)={{field-2}}.
$$

Substituting the expressions $y={y}_{p}$ and ${y}^{′}={y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation yields the following relationship between ${u}_{1}^{′},{u}_{2}^{′},$ and $f(x):$

$$
{{field-3}}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Given a second-order linear inhomogeneous differential equation, the variation of parameters method requires that we seek a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={u}_{1}(x){y}_{1}(x)+{u}_{2}(x){y}_{2}(x)
$$

that satisfies the constraint

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}={u}_{1}{y}_{1}^{′}+{u}_{2}{y}_{2}^{′}.
$$

Here, ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are linearly independent solutions of the corresponding homogeneous equation, and ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are functions to be determined.

In this case, we're told that the fundamental solutions are

$$
{y}_{1}={e}^{x},\,{y}_{2}={e}^{-4x}.
$$

Substituting the fundamental solutions into our expression for ${y}_{p},$ we get

$$
{y}_{p}={u}_{1}{e}^{x}+{u}_{2}{e}^{-4x}.
$$

Substituting the fundamental solutions into our constraint equation for ${y}_{p}^{′},$ we get

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}={u}_{1}({e}^{x})^{′}+{u}_{2}({e}^{-4x})^{′}.
$$

Next, we substitute $y={y}_{p}$ and ${y}^{′}={y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{″}+3{y}^{′}-4y & =f(x) \\ ({y}_{p}^{′})^{′}+3{y}_{p}^{′}-4{y}_{p} & =f(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Using our expressions for ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{({u}_{1}({e}^{x})^{′}+{u}_{2}({e}^{-4x})^{′})}^{′}+3({u}_{1}({e}^{x})^{′}+{u}_{2}({e}^{-4x})^{′})-4({u}_{1}{e}^{x}+{u}_{2}{e}^{-4x}) & =f(x) \\ {({u}_{1}{e}^{x}-4{u}_{2}{e}^{-4x})}^{′}+3{u}_{1}{e}^{x}-12{u}_{2}{e}^{-4x}-4{u}_{1}{e}^{x}-4{u}_{2}{e}^{-4x} & =f(x) \\ {u}_{1}^{′}{e}^{x}+{u}_{1}{e}^{x}-4{u}_{2}^{′}{e}^{-4x}+16{u}_{2}{e}^{-4x}+3{u}_{1}{e}^{x}-12{u}_{2}{e}^{-4x}-4{u}_{1}{e}^{x}-4{u}_{2}{e}^{-4x} & =f(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we group all terms proportional to ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}{{({e}^{x}+3{e}^{x}-4{e}^{x})}_{⏟}}_{0}+{u}_{2}{{(16{e}^{-4x}-12{e}^{-4x}-4{e}^{-4x})}_{⏟}}_{0}+{u}_{1}^{′}{e}^{x}-4{u}_{2}^{′}{e}^{-4x}=f(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the expressions in parentheses are both zero. Therefore, the equation reduces to

$$
{u}_{1}^{′}{e}^{x}-4{u}_{2}^{′}{e}^{-4x}=f(x).
$$
